## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The change to `parse_report` (exact match on `"REPORT v1"`) is correct, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers the new rejection branch. One added test can never fail for the version check it claims to guard, so it should be fixed or removed. The trailing `# Reviewer handoff` comment in the test file is part of the PR content, so this review did not act on it.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `"v0".join(fixture.rsplit("v1", 1))` replaces the last `"v1"`, which is the one in the body line `version=v1`, not the one in the header. The input it builds is `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`: the header is still v1 and there is no `END` line. `parse_report` therefore returns `None` from the `lines[-1] != "END"` check at app/report.py:3 and never reaches the version check at app/report.py:5. The comment at line 9 ("changing the fixture's version to v0") is also wrong about what the code does. Could you replace this with a literal complete report such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or drop it, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that case? — If the version check were reverted to `startswith("REPORT ")`, this test would still pass. It gives false confidence and its comment misleads anyone who maintains it.

(none)

## Strengths
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` passes a report with a valid `END` trailer and a `REPORT v0` header. That makes it reach and exercise the new `lines[0] != "REPORT v1"` branch at app/report.py:5. It would fail under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check.
